Commentable HTML

Plan with AI, visually rich review inline, repeat.

Comment on the exact sentence, cell, chart, diagram node, or code line, then paste one bundle back to the agent.

Prompt, review, and handoff in one file Works with Copilot and Claude One file you can keep or share
Act 1 - The promise

Point at the exact thing, then send one bundle back.

The garden plan is only the running example. What matters is the surface: prose, tables, charts, diagrams, code, and slides all become exact anchors an agent can act on - so you never have to describe "that part" in words.

  C1 --> P[Copy all, paste, press Enter]
  C2 --> P
  C3 --> P
  P -->|then repeat| H

Act 2 - Hand back only part of it

Send back the comments you choose, not always all of them.

Tick the ones you mean

Every comment card in the side pane carries a Select checkbox. Try it on this deck: comment on a couple of lines, open the panel, and tick one of them.

The picked card gets an accent ring, so a selection is obvious while you scan the list.

Copy selected

The moment something is picked, Copy all becomes Copy selected and a bar appears showing how many are chosen, with Clear selection beside it.

More > Clear selected comments deletes just those, leaving the rest of the review alone.

Useful when one round of feedback is ready to go and the rest is still being written - the bundle says it is a partial hand-back, so the agent never assumes the others were dealt with.

Supported syntax labels

The built-in highlighter covers the core review languages without a separate build step.

Python JavaScript TypeScript Bash PowerShell JSON YAML HTML CSS SQL Markdown +50 more 
def weekly_liters(bed, rainfall_mm=0.0):
    """Liters to add this week for one raised bed."""
    base = bed.area_m2 * 4.0
    note = "skip watering when rain covered the bed"
    if rainfall_mm >= 12.0:
        return 0.0
    return round(base - rainfall_mm * bed.area_m2, 1)

The diff renderer offers inline or side-by-side view. Code and KQL get line rows, copy buttons, and language-aware Copy all output.

Act 3 - How it fits your day

Three common review passes.

Review your own work

You and the agent. Generate the garden plan, mark what is off, Copy all, and let the agent tighten it before anyone else sees it.

Peer review

A teammate and you. Send a Shareable file. They comment in the file and send it back.

Review a plan before you build

Stakeholders and the agent. Walk a room through the plan, collect decisions on the board and checklist, and hand the agent one bundle of notes.

Act 4 - Behind the scenes

Anatomy of a commentable file.

One file, four stable ownership lanes

  • CSS region theme and layout rules the build can replace in one shot.
  • COMMENT UI region toolbar, sidebar, menus, and export chrome owned by the layer.
  • JS region runtime behavior, anchoring, exports, and widget logic.
  • CONTENT region your slides, report prose, diagrams, and examples - the part the author owns.

That separation is why upgrades stay deterministic: swap CSS, COMMENT UI, and JS, leave CONTENT alone, then re-stamp the version.

<main data-cmh-content-root data-cmh-mode="deck">
  <!-- BEGIN: CSS -->
  <!-- BEGIN: COMMENT UI -->
  <!-- BEGIN: JS -->
  <!-- BEGIN: CONTENT -->
  <section class="slide"> ... </section>
  <!-- END: CONTENT -->
</main>

The build swaps only the layer-owned regions and re-stamps the version. Your content is never clobbered.

Act 4 - Anchoring

How a comment finds the same spot on reload.

Text offsets

Prose and cells anchor by quote plus character range, resilient to small edits around them.

Structural keys

Charts, images, Mermaid nodes, and slides anchor by a stable element key, not a pixel position.

Widget deltas

Board moves and checklist toggles record the before and after state as part of the bundle.

Quote: "Bed 4 / Squash / 44 L"
Pinpoint: Act 2 > Evidence > watering table, row 2
Stable id: slide-d7119544::table-bed-4-liters
Note: make the high-water row easier to justify
HANDLED_IDS_JSON: ["cmh-bed4-liters"]

Stable ids let the agent mark a comment handled; on reload, handled-comment pruning clears it while unresolved notes stay put.

Act 4 - Safe by construction

How the skill is built.

Main skill file

SKILL.md is the entry point: when to use Commentable HTML, which authoring path to take, and which final validation steps are mandatory.

On-demand references

references/document-layout.md and references/design-decisions.md stay loaded on demand to keep context minimal until the agent needs that exact contract.

Deterministic editors

tools/authoring/new_document.py, tools/authoring/retrofit.py, and tools/authoring/upgrade.py do surgical, repeatable edits instead of freehand rewriting.

Mandatory final gate

tools/validate/validate.py --strict is the last stop before HTML goes back to the user, so malformed structure never slips through.

SKILL.md
references/document-layout.md
references/design-decisions.md
tools/authoring/retrofit.py
tools/validate/validate.py --strict deck-showcase.html
Act 4 - Validation methodology

Testing and validation keep the HTML honest.

UX-first browser checks

Playwright opens the real demos, clicks, drags, exports, and reloads them the way a reviewer does. plugin-tests.yml reruns that browser suite in CI.

Deterministic Python coverage

Python test_*.py files pin the builders, validators, and deck scaffolds so structure or safety regressions fail before publish.

Cross-platform and cross-agent

The repo reruns validators on Windows, macOS, and Linux, and the same shareable HTML works in Copilot and Claude because the output is just HTML.

Anti-regression by default

Every bug fix or new behavior adds a spec row and a covering test, so the next rebuild proves the contract still holds.
